summary:
The SP category is carrying this model right now, and today's slate hands it a loaded bench. R1 and R2 are both running 60% (105-70, n=175) on starting pitcher over the last 14 days, +7.5pts hot over their season baseline — and six games today feature full four-rating consensus, meaning SP signal stacks with trends/runs/bullpen agreement rather than fighting it. R3 and R4 are slightly cooler on SP (57%, 99-76) but still well above their season marks, so when all four ratings converge — as they do on TOR@KCR, BOS@BAL, DET@CLE, CHC@MIA, ATL@PHI, MIL@CIN, NYY@SDP and WSN@LAD — that's the SP-hot signal validating the pick, not just noise. Avoid leaning on bullpen_fatigue today; it's cold across the board at 41% (71-104, n=175) for R1/R2/R3, a -5.4pt drag, so any split game where fatigue is the tiebreaker (LAA@PIT, SFG@NYM, TBR@TEX, STL@COL, MIN@CHW, ARI@HOU, ATH@SEA) deserves a discount versus the consensus plays.

BOS@BAL is the single best game on the board by team trend: BOS as a liked side is 37-12 (76%) on the season and 20-6 (+18.0u) in strong-play spots, and today's rating gap is enormous and unanimous — R1 -1.35 through R4 -1.64, all favoring Boston on the road against BAL, a team the model has actually struggled backing lately (19-18, strong plays -4.0u). MIL@CIN is another value spot given MIL's 63% record (34-20) and +9.0u in strong plays, even though the delta here is modest (R4 -0.98) — shallower edge but a proven team-context tailwind. Elsewhere, DET@CLE shows the widest raw delta of the day (R1 +1.90) and full consensus, worth the largest unit if using R1/R2, since R1 is riding a nice recent groove (14d strong 41-31, +2.0u) after last week's bruising (7d -6.0u). Split games are where R4 stands out — it's on an incredible run (30d 62-38, 62%, +21.0u; 14d 59% hit rate), so on PIT, TEX, COL, CHW, HOU and SEA splits, give R4's read extra weight over the field.
